title: DATED: Guidelines for Creating Synthetic Datasets for Engineering Design Applications

bias_targets.methodology: Evaluating feature and label distributions using statistical methods, calculating spatial diversity (spread and uniformity), and measuring realism through similarity/distance metrics (e.g., Kullback-Leibler divergence, Hausdorff distance) between synthetic samples and real-world engineering data.

Assessing how large differences in numerical scale across features can artificially skew distance-based similarity calculations, and addressing it by computing measures within a normalized or standardized design space.

Analyzing the distribution of functional versus non-functional designs generated by different sampling techniques (e.g., random vs. diverse sampling) and evaluating their impact on the predictive performance of downstream machine learning classifiers across uniform, real, and specialized test sets.
